title: Tara's advice
introduction: Lady Tara is entered here. She is the granddaughter of Brihaspati, the Jupiter and wife of Vali and she is one of the exemplary females in this epic. She is entered only thrice in the vast of this epic, presently here, next at the fall of Vali and later to pacify the ire of Lakshmana. But her personality for analytical intelligence does not exit from the minds of readers. Here she advises Vali not to confront Sugreeva, as long as Rama stands guard to him. Further she says after a logical discourse and reasons, why not Sugreeva be made the Prince Regent of Kishkindha, even at this juncture, where she foresees a calamity to Vali. But Vali, maddened in his intellect by his brawny might slights her far fetching advice.
closing: इति वाल्मीकि रामायणे आदि काव्ये किष्किन्ध काण्डे पंचदशः सर्गः
Thus, this is the 15th chapter in Kishkindha Kanda of Valmiki Ramayana, the First Epic poem of India.

verses.devanagari:
अथ तस्य निनादम् तम् सुग्रीवस्य महात्मनः |
शुश्राव अन्तःपुर गतो वाली भ्रातुर् अमर्षणः
verses.iast:
atha tasya ninādam tam sugrīvasya mahātmanaḥ |
śuśrāva antaḥpura gato vālī bhrātur amarṣaṇaḥ
verses.translation: Then the illiberal Vali has clearly heard that outcry of his plain-spoken brother Sugreeva from his palace chambers.

glosses.meaning: to palace chambers, one who is in

verses.devanagari:
श्रुत्वा तु तस्य निनदम् सर्वभूत प्रकंपनम् |
मदः च एकपदे नष्टः क्रोधः च आपादितो महान्
verses.iast:
śrutvā tu tasya ninadam sarvabhūta prakampanam |
madaḥ ca ekapade naṣṭaḥ krodhaḥ ca āpādito mahān
verses.translation: On hearing Sugreeva's outcry that is shuddering all beings Vali's insolence is diminished as high furore superimposed on it.

verses.devanagari:
ततो रोष परीत अंगो वाली स कनक प्रभः |
उपरक्त इव आदित्यः सद्यो निष्प्रभताम् गतः
verses.iast:
tato roṣa parīta aṃgo vālī sa kanaka prabhaḥ |
uparak{}ta iva ādityaḥ sadyo niṣprabhatām gataḥ
verses.translation: Then, embitterment overspreading on all his limbs Vali with golden-hue is immediately rendered non-luminous like the eclipsed sun.

glosses.meaning: immediately, without, luminosity, went into [rendered as.]

verses.devanagari:
वाली दंष्ट्रा करालः तु क्रोधाद् दीप्त अग्नि लोचनः |
भाति उत्पतित पद्माभः समृणाल इव ह्रदः
verses.iast:
vālī daṃṣṭrā karālaḥ tu krodhād dīpta agni locanaḥ |
bhāti utpatita padmābhaḥ samṛṇāla iva hradaḥ
verses.translation: With asymmetrical teeth and with burning fireball like eyes Vali is reflective of a lake whose red-lotuses are uprooted leaving stalks afloat.
notes: Vali's aspect is like a lake into which an elephant on its entry creates turmoil and uproots its red-lotuses, thus leaving the pond with their stalks afloat and its clear water turning reddish due to the elephant's heaving of the slushy red-mud. Maheshvara Tiirtha.

glosses.meaning: with, stalks, lake, like bhaati = he shone forth.

verses.devanagari:
शब्दम् दुर्मर्षणम् श्रुत्वा निष्पपात ततो हरिः |
वेगेन च पद न्यासैर् दारयन् इव मेदिनीम्
verses.iast:
śabdam durmarṣaṇam śrutvā niṣpapāta tato hariḥ |
vegena ca pada nyāsair dārayan iva medinīm
verses.translation: That monkey Vali then on hearing that intolerable noise bolted out of palace chambers thumping his feet as though to shatter the earth.

verses.devanagari:
तम् तु तारा परिष्वज्य स्नेहाद् दर्शित सौहृदा |
उवाच त्रस्त संभ्रांता हित उदर्कम् इदम् वचः
verses.iast:
tam tu tārā pariṣvajya snehād darśita sauhṛdā |
uvāca trasta sambhrāṃtā hita udarkam idam vacaḥ
verses.translation: His wife Tara stepped in and showing goodwill and amity hugged him, for she is in fear and bewilderment, and said this word that is beneficial in its futurity if Vali heeds it.

glosses.meaning: one who has shown, good will

verses.devanagari:
साधु क्रोधम् इमम् वीर नदी वेगम् इव आगतम् |
शयनाद् उत्थितः काल्यम् त्यज भुक्ताम् इव स्रजम्
verses.iast:
sādhu krodham imam vīra nadī vegam iva āgatam |
śayanād utthitaḥ kālyam tyaja bhuk{}tām iva srajam
verses.translation: "Oh brave one, you better gently leave off this anger that is coming on like a gushing river as is done with an enjoyed chaplet on getting up from bed in early hours.

verses.devanagari:
काल्यम् एतेन संग्रामम् करिष्यसि च वानर |
वीर ते शत्रु बाहुल्यम् फल्गुता वा न विद्यते
verses.iast:
kālyam etena saṅgrāmam kariṣyasi ca vānara |
vīra te śatru bāhulyam phalgutā vā na vidyate
verses.translation: "Oh, monkey, you can fight with him in early hours of tomorrow, oh, brave one, evidently you neither have divers enemies nor your valour is trivialised."
notes: Fighting on next day morning means that Sugreeva has come in the evening time. This is not accepted by some and they give meaning to the word kālyam differently.

glosses.meaning: with him, in early hours / or at appropriate time, fighting, you can do

verses.devanagari:
सहसा तव निष्क्रामो मम तावत् न रोचते |
श्रूयताम् अभिधास्यामि यन् निमित्तम् निवार्यते
verses.iast:
sahasā tava niṣkrāmo mama tāvat na rocate |
śrūyatām abhidhāsyāmi yan nimittam nivāryate
verses.translation: "Your quick exiting is disagreeable for me, and what for you are dissuaded that may be listened as I tell.

glosses.meaning: by what, reason, you are dissuaded
let it be heard, I will tell.

verses.devanagari:
पूर्वम् आपतितः क्रोधात् स त्वाम् आह्वयते युधि |
निष्पत्य च निरस्तः ते हन्यमानो दिशो गतः
verses.iast:
pūrvam āpatitaḥ krodhāt sa tvām āhvayate yudhi |
niṣpatya ca nirastaḥ te hanyamāno diśo gataḥ
verses.translation: "Earlier Sugreeva came assaulting and inviting you for a combat, and you also have gone out and rendered him as a nonentity, and being battered by you he fled in all directions.

glosses.meaning: earlier, in anger came, falling on - came assaulting
you, for fight, he is inviting
by you, being battered, into directions, fled.

verses.devanagari:
त्वया तस्य निरस्तस्य पीडितस्य विशेषतः |
इह एत्य पुनर् आह्वानम् शंकाम् जनयति इव मे
verses.iast:
tvayā tasya nirastasya pīḍitasya viśeṣataḥ |
iha etya punar āhvānam śaṃkām janayati iva me
verses.translation: "He who is undone earlier by you, particularly after torturing by you, his coming here again and inviting you for a duel is causing a doubt in me.

glosses.meaning: to me, doubt, causing, like that.

verses.devanagari:
दर्पः च व्यवसायः च यादृशः तस्य नर्दतः |
निनादस्य च संरंभो न एतत् अल्पम् हि कारणम्
verses.iast:
darpaḥ ca vyavasāyaḥ ca yādṛśaḥ tasya nardataḥ |
ninādasya ca saṃrambho na etat alpam hi kāraṇam
verses.translation: "The arrogance and endeavour of the shouter, and even the rampage of his furore, all these will not have a trivial reason, isn't it.

glosses.meaning: all this, with trivial, reason, not, isn't it.

verses.devanagari:
न असहायम् अहम् मन्ये सुग्रीवम् तम् इह आगतम् |
अवष्टब्ध सहायः च यम् आश्रित्य एष गर्जति
verses.iast:
na asahāyam aham manye sugrīvam tam iha āgatam |
avaṣṭabdha sahāyaḥ ca yam āśritya eṣa ga.rjati
verses.translation: "I do not think that Sugreeva has come here unaccompanied, and on whom he is dependant must be an unflinching support foregathered by Sugreeva.

glosses.meaning: to here, who came, that, Sugreeva is
whom, depending on, he is [Sugreeva is,] roaring.

verses.devanagari:
प्रकृत्या निपुणः चैव बुद्धिमान् चैव वानरः |
न अपरीक्षित वीर्येण सुग्रीवः सख्यम् एष्यति
verses.iast:
prakṛtyā nipuṇaḥ caiva buddhimān caiva vānaraḥ |
na aparīkṣita vīryeṇa sugrīvaḥ sakhyam eṣyati
verses.translation: "By his nature Sugreeva is an expert and even so a clever one, and he does not enter into friendship with anyone without examining his mettle.

glosses.meaning: by nature, [Sugreeva is] an expert, also thus

verses.devanagari:
पूर्वम् एव मया वीर श्रुतम् कथयतो वचः |
अंगदस्य कुमारस्य वक्ष्यामि अद्य हितम् वचः
verses.iast:
pūrvam eva mayā vīra śrutam kathayato vacaḥ |
aṃgadasya kumārasya vakṣyāmi adya hitam vacaḥ
verses.translation: "I am already briefed by our son Angada's information, and what I have heard I will now relate that helpful word to you.

glosses.meaning: helpful, word, now, I will tell.

verses.devanagari:
अंगदः तु कुमरो अयम् वनांतम् उपनिर्गतः |
प्रवृत्तिः तेन कथिता चारैः असीत् निवेदिता
verses.iast:
aṃgadaḥ tu kumaro ayam vanāṃtam upanirgataḥ |
pravṛttiḥ tena kathitā cāraiḥ asīt niveditā
verses.translation: "Son Angada said this account when he returned from forests, and to him spies are said to have reported this.

glosses.meaning: in forest, interior, [went and] came out of
by him, an account, is said

verses.devanagari:
अयोध्य अधिपतेः पुत्रौ शूरौ समर दुर्जयौ |
इक्ष्वाकूणाम् कुले जातौ प्रथितौ राम लक्ष्मणौ
सुग्रीव प्रिय कामार्थम् प्राप्तौ तत्र दुरासदौ |
verses.iast:
ayodhya adhipateḥ putrau śūrau samara durjayau |
ikśvākūṇām kule jātau prathitau rāma lakśmaṇau
sugrīva priya kāmārtham prāptau tatra durāsadau |
verses.translation: "Those that are born in Ikshvaku dynasty, sons of the king of Ayodhya, valiant and unconquerable ones in war, called Rama and Lakshmana are there in this country. These two unassailable ones have chanced there at Sugreeva's place to fulfil the longing desire of Sugreeva.

glosses.meaning: are available [and moving in this country]
those two being not, assailable ones

verses.devanagari:
स ते भ्रातुर् हि विख्यातः सहायो रण कर्मणि
रामः पर बलमर्दी युगान्त अग्निः इव उत्थितः |
verses.iast:
sa te bhrātur hi vikhyātaḥ sahāyo raṇa ka.rmaṇi
rāmaḥ para balamardī yugānta agniḥ iva utthitaḥ |
verses.translation: "He is an acclaimed one for his warfare, and like the fire flaring up at the end of era he shatters the strength of enemies, and he is Rama your brother's helpmate, they say so.

glosses.meaning: flared up, era, end of, fire, like
your, brother's, helpmate, they say so.

verses.devanagari:
निवास वृक्षः साधूनाम् आपन्नानाम् परा गतिः |
आर्तानाम् संश्रयः चैव यशसः च एक भाजनम् |
verses.iast:
nivāsa vṛkṣaḥ sādhūnām āpannānām parā gatiḥ |
ārtānām saṃśrayaḥ caiva yaśasaḥ ca eka bhājanam |
verses.translation: "And he is said to the habitable tree for the polite, the ultimate course for the woebegone, a hospice for the agonised, and for grace Rama is the only abode.

glosses.meaning: for the polite, a habitable, tree
for grace, also, the only, abode.

verses.devanagari:
ज्ञान विज्ञान संपन्नो निदेशो निरतः पितुः
धातूनाम् इव शैलेन्द्रो गुणानाम् आकरो महान् |
verses.iast:
jñāna vijñāna sampanno nideśo nirataḥ pituḥ
dhātūnām iva śailendro guṇānām ākaro mahān |
verses.translation: "He is endowed with the knowledge of mundane and ultra-mundane things, he always abides in the directives of his father, and as with Mt. Himalayas for all natural elements he is the greatest mine of merits.

glosses.meaning: knowledge [of mundane things,] knowledge [of ultra-mundane things,] endowed with
abides] = in father's, directive, always involved, [or, one who abides]
for elements, like, mountain, the great -Himalayas

verses.devanagari:
तत् क्षमो न विरोधः ते सह तेन महात्मना
दुर्जयेन अप्रमेयेण रामेण रण कर्मसु |
verses.iast:
tat kṣamo na virodhaḥ te saha tena mahātmanā
durjayena aprameyeṇa rāmeṇa raṇa karmasu |
verses.translation: "By that reason, with that unconquerable on in conflicts, an imponderable one and a great-soul Rama, your enmity is inapposite.
notes: For the above three stanzas very lengthy commentary is rendered of which some points are detailed here. Lady Tara is elucidating the whole being of Rama as gathered by her from her son Angada. The second foot of verse 19 starts with the words nivāsa vṛkśa a habitable tree; if it be asked why Rama is compared with a tree, then it is said that tree requires no formalities like 'may I come in...' or 'rights of admission reserved...' etc., as with any other house or habitation, for taking hold of its shade. A tree first gives its shade to the traveller who seeks it and then affords its fruits or flowers satisfying the basic needs of the needy. So Rama is such a tree that protects and nourishes, should anybody seek his grace.

Next is sādhūnām for polite supplicants he is the ultimate course. Tara is saying indirectly that Vali is not at all polite in treating Sugreeva either as crown prince of Kishkindha or as his own younger brother. As such Vali cannot supplicate to Rama at this stage for his impoliteness to Sugreeva and to Ruma, wife of Sugreeva, which is intolerable to Rama, and hence Vali shall not confront Rama. ārtānām for earnest and anguished supplicants Rama is the ultimate recourse. This is what later said in Bhagavat Gita at 9-22, yoga skhemam vahamyaham... Vali may dismiss this idea saying that 'if Rama is the ultimate course for the polite supplicants, I have my recourse to other supreme lords, i.e., none other than Indra, my father...' And for this Tara is supplementing her thought in saying, yaśasaḥ ca eka bhājanaḥ the grace Rama is the only ultimate abode, where Indra and others are but penultimate. Hence as long as Rama is standing guard to Sugreeva, Sugreeva cannot be trivialised and this again as said in Bhagavad Gita, na me bhaktaḥ praṇaśyati... at 9-31.

Alternately, it is again as said later in Gita at 7-16 that caturvidhā bhajante mām... 'four kinds of devotees worship me...' Those four are, one who is seeking knowledge sādhūnām; those that are interested in salvation, kaivalya kāmuka; like King Priikshit. One seeking of material gains āpannānām; those that seek the material gains that were not there previously to them, also called artha ardhī; like Sugreeva, Dhruva. One who is distraught ārtānām; those that are in anguish like Gajendra, the Elephant caught in lake by crocodile in gajendra mokśa. And the fourthly one who is a wise person yaśasaḥ jñāni; gloriously enlightened one, like Shuka, Sanaka, Naarada, Bhiishma, Prahlada. And this wise one is impossible to exist and if he is there 'he is my soul jñānī tu ātmaiva me matam...' Gita 7-18.For all these four kinds Rama is ...eka bhājanam..., the only recourse.

Next is jñāna, vijñāna sampatti In that jñāna is privy to the materialistic, worldly, kingly affairs. vijñāna is the knowledge derived from the scriptures, providentially profound. Or, through karmadhāraya, jñānaḥ ca asau vijñā sampannaḥ ca... corporeally he is the knowledge, and spiritually he is gnostic as well. Hence he is the phenomenon of the Supreme Being in maintaining dharma. In order to maintain that dharma Rama is now observant of his father's orders pituḥ nideśe nirataḥ. This pursuit of father's orders is but one of the many other attributes of his dharma, and that alone is said here as secondary attribute, upa lakśaṇa. Hence in pursuing his dharma Rama may eradicate adharma of Vali, insofar as Vali's misdemeanours towards Sugreeva and his wife Ruma are concerned. guṇānām ākaraḥ; with his auspicious merits he is a Great Mine. Usually these guṇa-s, attributs of Vishnu are six as per Vaishnavaite classification, con solidating them as ṣaḍguṇa sampatti , which are aiśvarya, vīrya, yaśas, śrī, jñāna, vairāgya. And there are many more in the depth of the soul of Rama hitherto unexcavated. As such, there are innumerable and auspicious elements, or merits, in him dhātūnām śailendraḥ. These elements neither subdivide nor shake him off his Himalayan personality, in the pursuit to establish dharma.

glosses.meaning: your, enmity, not, admissible - inadmissible, inappropriate, inapposite.

verses.devanagari:
शूर वक्ष्यामि ते किंचिन् न च इच्छामि अभ्यसूयितुम्
श्रूयताम् क्रियताम् चैव तव वक्ष्यामि यद् हितम् |
verses.iast:
śūra vakṣyāmi te kiñcin na ca icchāmi abhyasūyitum
śrūyatām kriyatām caiva tava vakṣyāmi yad hitam |
verses.translation: "Oh dauntless one, I tell you this much that you shall not become overcritical of him, and what I say is beneficial to you that may now be listened and even implemented.

glosses.meaning: to you, a little, I will say
you to find fault in good merits, you to become overcritical
to you, what that is beneficial, that, I am saying

verses.devanagari:
यौवराज्येन सुग्रीवम् तूर्णम् साधु अभिषेचय
विग्रहम् मा कृथा वीर भ्रात्रा राजन् यवीयसा |
verses.iast:
yauvarājyena sugrīvam tūrṇam sādhu abhiṣecaya
vigraham mā kṛthā vīra bhrātrā rājan yavīyasā |
verses.translation: "Oh, king, let Sugreeva be decorously and quickly anointed as prince regent, and oh, resolute one, let there be no hostility to your own younger brother.

verses.devanagari:
अहम् हि ते क्षमम् मन्ये तेन रामेण सौहृदम्
सुग्रीवेण च संप्रीतिम् वैरम् उत्सृज्य दूरतः |
verses.iast:
aham hi te kṣamam manye tena rāmeṇa sauhṛdam
sugrīveṇa ca samprītim vairam utsṛjya dūrataḥ |
verses.translation: "Achieving unanimity with Sugreeva and solidarity with Rama by discarding enmity, in effect is appropriate for you, thus I deem.

glosses.meaning: to you, appropriate, I, deem, in effect.

verses.devanagari:
लालनीयो हि ते भ्राता यवीयान् एष वानरः
तत्र वा सन्निहस्थो वा सर्वथा बन्धुः एव ते |
verses.iast:
lālanīyo hi te bhrātā yavīyān eṣa vānaraḥ
tatra vā sannihastho vā sarvathā bandhuḥ eva te |
verses.translation: "This Sugreeva is your younger brother and you should be keen about him, isn't it... and whether he is here or there in Rishyamuka he is just your brother.

glosses.meaning: to you, to be keen about him, isn't it
in any way, kinsman, just, of yours.

verses.devanagari:
नहि तेन समम् बन्धुम् भुवि पश्यामि किंचन
दान मानादि सत्कर्रैः कुरुष्व प्रत्यनन्तरम् |
वैरम् एतत् सम् उत्स्रृज्य तव पार्श्वे स तिष्ठतु
verses.iast:
nahi tena samam bandhum bhuvi paśyāmi kiñcana
dāna mānādi satkarraiḥ kuruṣva pratyanantaram |
vairam etat sam ut.hsrṛjya tava pārśve sa tiṣṭhatu
verses.translation: "Indeed, I do not see anyone on earth a coequal to him in kindred spirit, hence leave off this enmity and honour him with bestowals and felicitations as an insider, and retain him at your side.

glosses.meaning: on earth, not, I see, indeed
all this, enmity, completely leaving off
with bestowals, felicitations, and the like, honours
like one who is very close / like one who is your legatee
him, by your, side, be kept.

verses.devanagari:
सुग्रीवो विपुल ग्रीवो महाबन्धुः मतः तव |
भ्रातृ सौहृदम् आलंब्य न अन्या गति इह अस्ति ते
verses.iast:
sugrīvo vipula grīvo mahābandhuḥ mataḥ tava |
bhrātṛ sauhṛdam ālambya na anyā gati iha asti te
verses.translation: "That boisterously voiced Sugreeva is indisputably an excellent kinsman of yours, and hence brace yourself with the fondness of brotherhood, as there is no other way out to you.

glosses.meaning: your, an excellent, kinsman, accepted as - indisputable kinsman

glosses.itrans: te iha anyaa gati na asti
glosses.iast: te iha anyā gati na asti
glosses.devanagari: ते इह अन्या गति न अस्ति
glosses.meaning: to you, now, another, way out, is not, there.

verses.devanagari:
यदि ते मत् प्रियम् कार्यम् यदि च अवैषि माम् हिताम् |
याच्यमानः प्रियत्वेन साधु वाक्यम् कुरुष्व मे
verses.iast:
yadi te mat priyam kāryam yadi ca avaiṣi mām hitām |
yācyamānaḥ priyatvena sādhu vākyam kuruṣva me
verses.translation: "If you look upon to do my favoured deed, and if you look upon me as an expedient one, I beg of you in our loving attachment that my gentle word of advise be done.

glosses.meaning: to you, to me, dear, deed [if you consider,] if
me, as expedient, means of attaining an end, [if you] believe, if
my, word [of advise,] simply, you make happen.

verses.devanagari:
प्रसीद पथ्यम् श्रुणु जल्पितम् हि मे
न रोषम् एव अनुविधातुम् अर्हसि |
क्षमो हि ते कोशल राज सूनुना
न विग्रहः शक्र सम तेजसा
verses.iast:
prasīda pathyam śruṇu jalpitam hi me
na roṣam eva anuvidhātum arhasi |
kśamo hi te kośala rāja sūnunā
na vigrahaḥ śakra sama tejasā
verses.translation: "Be graceful and it behove you to listen to my small but expedient talk, and following up rancour alone is unbecoming of you, thereby your confrontation with the Prince of Kosala will be unpardonable for his dynamism equals that of Indra." Thus Tara spoke to her husband Vali.

glosses.meaning: listen, to my, expedient, small talk
to follow up, not, becoming of you
to you, confrontation, not, pardonable, indeed.

verses.devanagari:
तदा हि तारा हितम् एव वाक्यम्
तम् वालिनम् पथ्यम् इदम् बभाषे |
न रोचते तद् वचनम् हि तस्य
काल अभिपन्नस्य विनाश काले
verses.iast:
tadā hi tārā hitam eva vākyam
tam vālinam pathyam idam babhāṣe |
na rocate tad vacanam hi tasya
kāla abhipannasya vināśa kāle
verses.translation: Then, though Tara spoke beneficial and advisable words they are unimpressive to Vali for he is impounded by fatality and driven by time to his doom.
